header.title: Ultra-low China datacenter build cost and power accelerate capacity buildout

s01_bottom_line.text: China builds hyperscale datacenters very fast and cheap: Galaxy's first 120MW phase was delivered within a year at a fifth of US costs; capex has fallen ~25% to under $3mm/MW, rents roughly halved to ~$40/kW/month, and Inner Mongolia power is ~$0.055/kWh; the region has 25GW of announced projects. ⟨cited figures: approximate⟩
The article shows China can build hyperscale campuses at a fraction of US cost and on fast timelines, offering a reference point for the US roadmap and documenting a large accelerating buildout.

Falling build costs, cheap power and abundant labor support a large accelerating datacenter buildout in Inner Mongolia, but the article does not quantify the earnings impact for any listed supplier and notes thin project returns.
